questions.q: What changed when the printing press arrived, according to the summary?
a: Information could be stored outside the mind
People gradually lost the ability to read
Books became too expensive for most people
Memory contests were banned in Europe
questions.why: Lesson 1 says external storage reduced the need to remember things, and memory has declined since.

questions.q: How did the test subject S.F. improve his digit memory?
a: By repeating sequences to himself for hundreds of hours
By using a memory palace built in childhood
By writing numbers down every night
By learning a new language before the test
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he raised his span from 7 to 79 digits through over 230 hours of repetition.

questions.q: What does the summary say about chess players' memory?
a: It works for chess positions but not general tests
It transfers to every kind of memory task
It comes from memorizing opening books
It is no better than an average person's
questions.why: Lesson 2 says chess memory is limited to chess and does not help with general memory tests.

questions.q: What is chunking, as described in the summary?
a: Breaking one long string of information into smaller parts
Repeating information aloud until it sticks
Linking facts to places you know well
Reviewing material at increasing intervals
questions.why: Lesson 3 shows a long number becoming two memorable dates when split into chunks.

questions.q: How does the memory palace technique work?
a: You place items along a route you know well
You group numbers into meaningful dates
You repeat each item seven times in a row
You write items on cards and shuffle them
questions.why: Lesson 3 says you walk a familiar route and store memories in specific locations along it.
